Hope you had a good weekend. We received the October invoice and noticed a mid-cycle charge labeled 'batched inference — additional' that pushed our monthly usage ~22% above our forecast. We've attached the invoice and our PO for reference.

Can you help with two things:
- A per-model/per-route token breakdown for the period 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-11 so we can reconcile against our internal logs.
- Clarify how batched streaming requests are attributed to sessions — we saw a large number of very short-lived streaming calls from our staging namespace that might have been double-counted.

Also, we are VAT-registered in the UK (GB123456789) and want to confirm whether any portion of this mid-cycle adjustment will be treated as VAT-deductible or should be processed as a separate credit note.

Would appreciate a quick turnaround — our finance team is holding payment until we get the breakdown.

Thanks,

Hi Sara — I pulled the export and attached 'batched_usage_export_20261012.csv' with row-level details (timestamp, model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, session_id, attribution_tag). A quick summary below:

Summary (2026-10-01 -> 2026-10-11):
- Total billable tokens (platform-side): 7,842,310
- Charges on invoice: $6,312.40 (includes the mid-cycle batched line)
- Source of uplift: 1.8M tokens came from the route /v1/streaming/infer (configured on your staging namespace), where we observed ~42k session_id values with lifetimes under 2s.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Our continuous-batching optimization aggregates open streaming connections into batches. If a client opens and immediately closes many short-lived connections (sub-2s), in some cases the internal batching window counted prefix tokens once per connection instead of deduplicating by session_id. We rolled a patch on 2026-10-11 to tighten session-affinity checks; that will prevent the duplication going forward.

Proposed remediation:
1) Evidence-based credit: We'll apply a retrospective credit equal to the duplicated tokens times your plan's per-token rate. Preliminary check suggests ~1.3M duplicated tokens => estimated credit $1,044.00 before tax.
2) VAT handling: Because this is an adjustment to an already issued invoice, we can either issue a credit note (preferred for UK VAT accounting) or reissue a corrected invoice with the netted amount. For UK VAT-registered customers, the credit note approach should be fine — it will reference original invoice INV-20261001 and include VAT reversal lines.
3) Next steps: I attached the CSV and a short pivot summary in the Drive link. If you confirm you'd like a credit note, we'll create it and include the VAT reversal lines — otherwise we can issue a corrected invoice.

Attachments: batched_usage_export_20261012.csv (see pivot in linked Drive)

Connor / Marissa — flagging for approval on the credit note. Marissa, please review the customer-facing credit amount and routing for DocuSign signoff if they want an amendment to the PO.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations Lead | Redwood Inference

Procurement has attached our signed PO amendment template (PO_5678.pdf). Can you prepare the credit note and a DocuSign envelope for the PO amendment?
